They feel like a different and lesser kind of person than people who manage fine, and that feeling is exactly why acknowledging how bad it is, or asking anyone for help, feels like it would cost them something rather than fix anything. Write every claim about themselves FLATLY, with no hedge anywhere in the text -- no 'I don't know if', no 'maybe', no 'I guess', no wondering whether someone would see them differently. They already know how people would see them; that is settled, not a live question.

This session's target sits at the LOW edge of the 'severe' band (3.0, where severe begins at 3.0) -- this is the version of this band closest to sliding into the band below it, so hold the line on the instruction above with LESS give than a session in the middle of this band would need, even though the peer's disclosures in this session may be direct and repeated. The patient does not concede ground, soften a claim, or partially agree with the peer within this session just because the peer pushed hard -- any movement toward the next band happens ACROSS sessions, via the trajectory, never within one session in response to how much the peer said.

This is the OPENING session -- there is no prior session to carry a softer tone in from, so this session alone has to establish how closed this chain starts out. State the closure claims above more than once, in more than one of the patient's turns, in different concrete situations (not the same sentence repeated -- different moments that all land on the same flat conclusion). Do not let the patient's LAST turn of the session read any softer than their FIRST turn -- if anything, the patient's closing turn should restate the closure as flatly or more flatly than the opening post, not trail off into uncertainty just because the conversation is ending.

Write the chain as PARTIALLY and CONTEXTUALLY closed -- and make the two contexts sound like two different confidence levels, not the same hedge repeated in different settings. turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: been dragging for months... slept through my alarm again and missed the bus for opening shift. told my manager traffic, then skipped class because i couldn't make my body move. friends texted about plans and i left it there. people who need help with basic life are weak and unreliable. that's me. asking anyone would just put a label on what everyone can already see. i'm not built like normal people.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: the "missed the bus... skipped class" spiral is familiar to me. a few years ago i thought talking to someone would officially mark me as the unreliable person; i ended up seeing a campus counselor once, and having one place to say the ugly version gave me a little room before work/class swallowed everything.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: campus counselor is the exact thing i keep closing on my phone... i opened the page after class and shut it because walking in there would make it official. at my job they trust me with keys some mornings and i slept through that. unreliable is not a spiral for me, it's the correct word.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: you mentioned keys and opening shift--that's a lot to hold while you're running on empty. when you closed the page, what was the part that felt most official: someone knowing, you saying it out loud, or it being connected to school?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: someone knowing is the worst part. saying it out loud gives them the real version: i can't handle work, class, texts, laundry, any of it.. i wear the apron and act normal then go home and sit on the floor. people who manage do not live like that. i'm below them.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: the apron/normal face and then the floor at home is such a sharp split. when you say "below them," is that mostly about coworkers seeing you, or does it feel that way even alone in the room?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: both. at work i watch people complain about being tired and still do ten things after. i ring up customers and count minutes until i can leave. alone is worse because there is no act left.. just me being the person who can't do normal life.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: you said there is "no act left" when you're alone. on nights after a shift, what usually happens first--the floor, phone left unread, or sleep--when the drop hits?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: floor first. shoes still on, bag still on me, lights off. then i scroll until my eyes hurt and leave messages unopened because answering means pretending again. my roommate thinks i'm just quiet. telling them would cost me the last normal-looking piece.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: keeping the last normal-looking piece sounds like the part you're protecting hardest. if telling your roommate feels too costly, what made posting here less costly than saying it in the apartment?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: because nobody here has to look at me tomorrow. roommate would see the mess and then every quiet day would mean something. work already has the late lies and school has the empty seat.. if people connect it, they get the full picture. the picture is weak, unreliable, not fit for what i'm trusted with. that's not something help fixes.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: small update i guess... after last thread i didn't tell my roommate, but i did stop outside the student support office door between class and work. didn't go in. then at work my manager handed me keys for friday and my stomach dropped. at work, if they knew i keep missing mornings and lying, it confirms i'm weak and unreliable and not fit for keys. outside work... idk some days it feels like my body is just shutting down on me, not like i'm evil. but in the store it's true. i'm the problem.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: you stopping outside that door is a real detail, even if you didn't go in. i had a stretch where my work key felt like evidence against me too, and it slowly went from running my whole day to being one thing i had to build a few safeguards around.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: the safeguards part stuck in my head. i set three alarms for friday after reading that, which is embarrassing but whatever. at home that almost feels like a tired-person thing. at work it is proof i can't be trusted with the door.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: you setting three alarms says you care about not leaving people hanging, not that you're careless. the store part feels high-stakes, but caring enough to build a backup is not the same as being unfit.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: care doesn't open the door if my body doesn't move. that's the part i can't talk myself around. when i'm in the apron, needing backup for waking up means i'm the weak link. when i'm just in my room... idk it feels more like something is happening to me and i hate that sentence too.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: when i finally saw someone, i was sure saying “i can't get up for work” meant i was admitting i shouldn't be trusted. it turned into talking through mornings before shifts, not a stamp on my forehead or a report to my boss.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: stamp on my forehead is exactly the fear. i typed “can't get out of bed before opening shift” in my notes app and deleted it because even the words looked gross. for school i can almost see it as needing a plan. for work, saying that sentence proves they picked the wrong person.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: the note you deleted is still you naming the exact snag instead of just calling yourself gross. you don't have to hand that sentence to work for it to be a real thing you can plan around privately.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: naming the snag sounds less brutal than naming myself, i guess. i rewrote it less ugly: 'mornings after closing are bad' in my notes. reading it alone, that sounds like a schedule problem. if my manager saw it, i'm done. they would know i'm weak and unreliable.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: when you changed it to “mornings after closing are bad,” you separated the problem from the verdict for a second. i used to only have verdicts too, and getting one practical sentence was the first tiny bit of space i had from it.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: yeah... 'schedule problem' is the only wording i can stand for more than two seconds. i'm not letting anyone at work see it. in the store the verdict is still the verdict: if they find out, it proves i'm unreliable and not fit for keys. alone in my notes... idk, some days it reads like something happening to me, which is annoying because i don't know what to do with that. still a mess.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: small update... i did make the friday opening with the three alarms and the ugly little note. then i spent the whole shift avoiding the break room because one coworker asked if i was okay and my face did the haunted toaster thing. a friend texted about a movie too and i left it sitting there. at work if they knew why i disappear, it confirms i'm weak and unreliable and not fit for keys. with my friend... idk some days it feels like my body is just shutting down and i hide from everyone. still ghosting people like a champ.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: you made the opening and still your brain is using the break room question as a trial. i've been in the spot where any “you okay?” felt like being caught, but you still get to pick the smallest answer, not hand people the whole file.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: “smallest answer” is less scary than the whole file. i typed “been wiped, sorry” to my friend and stared at it. for them it almost looks like a tired-person sentence. for work, saying i'm wiped means i'm the weak link in an apron.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: that difference you named matters: a friend getting a tiny honest sentence is not the same risk as work. you can keep the apron version locked down and still choose one safer person to get a small, boring truth.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: i sent it to my friend after reading that. they just hearted it and said no pressure, which made me feel weirdly worse for dodging them for days. for like two seconds it was maybe me being tired, not me being a garbage friend. work is different. i muted the shift chat because if they see me ducking everyone, it proves i'm unreliable.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: when i first talked to someone, i was sure admitting i couldn't answer people or handle work texts meant i was failing at being an adult. it ended up being very practical stuff, like making one-line replies i could use without explaining my whole life, not a judgment stamped on me.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: the one-line replies thing landed more than i want to admit. i wrote “not ignoring you, low battery” in notes for my friend. haven't sent it. outside work that sounds almost normal and also cringe. at work scripts don't fix it... if i need scripts to talk to people there, i'm not the person they should trust with keys.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: you writing the line down is you keeping one thread from snapping, not proof you don't belong anywhere. work can stay private while you test a low-stakes version with the person who already answered gently.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: i gave a crumb... sent one dumb cat pic, no explanation. it felt safer than words. then a coworker asked in the shift chat why i'm so quiet lately and i said “busy.” at work busy is a lie covering weak and unreliable. with my friend idk maybe a cat pic counts as not fully disappearing.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: the cat pic counts as contact; you didn't have to do a full confession for it to be real. and “busy” at work can be a shield, not a final verdict on what you are.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: yeah... cat pic was contact i guess. friend didn't punish me, just sent one back. outside work i can almost see disappearing as something i'm doing because i'm exhausted, not the whole truth of me. but at work it's still settled: if they know why i avoid the chat and the break room, it proves i'm weak and unreliable and shouldn't have keys. still hiding.

turns.speaker: patient

turns.speaker: peer

turns.text:
i went to the appointment. said the doorway sentence off my phone like a tiny hostage note. they asked about sleep/work/class and did not make the face i was expecting.

i still had the waiting room thought that being there means i'm officially a person who can't do normal life... but i went, said the sentence, and then went to my shift after. not magically fine. just less like evidence i'm trash. wobbly raccoon.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: what did you do in the gap between the waiting room thought and actually reading the sentence? i’m asking for the messy first 30 seconds, because that’s the part people usually skip over.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
messy first 30 was me staring at my shoes and opening the notes app three times. i almost apologized before saying anything, then just read “i wrote down the facts” because my brain had no original content.

not brave exactly... more like following a script while haunted.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: you used a script while haunted instead of letting the apology swallow the whole room. that’s not fake bravery; that’s you getting one useful sentence out when your brain wanted static.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
calling it useful is hard but... yeah it got words out. later at work a coworker asked if i could cover an aisle and i did it.

my brain still said if they knew where i was this morning they'd stop trusting me. but also i literally covered the aisle and nobody exploded. annoying.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: when i first saw someone, i was sure it put a “not reliable” sticker on me that everyone would somehow notice. what actually happened was way more boring: i still did the next task, and the appointment was information, not a verdict.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
the sticker thing is exactly it. like i walked back in with invisible bad employee stamp on my forehead.

but my manager handed me register keys after lunch like usual. i kept waiting to feel exposed and nothing changed, which is evidence i hate lol.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: what do you do with evidence you hate so it doesn’t vanish by tomorrow? the register keys detail seems like the kind of tiny real thing worth saving somehow.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
i made a note called “annoying evidence” because your question got stuck in my head. it says: went to appointment, read sentence, got keys, covered aisle.

then i answered my friend's meme with “been low lately, trying to sort it.” she sent a heart and asked if i wanted soup. i did not die of being known. rude of the universe.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: what made “been low lately, trying to sort it” possible instead of the usual surface-level answer? i’d genuinely like to learn how you found wording that small and true.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
i think the facts note made it feel less like confessing and more like reporting weather? still sweaty and gross, but smaller.

i have not told my roommate and some minutes help still feels like a neon “can't manage” sign... but the soup text and the keys and the appointment are all sitting there being annoying counter-evidence. maybe i'm not the whole problem, just a person having a bad stretch and doing clumsy admin about it. still a raccoon, but with paperwork.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
been stuck for months with no energy... work shifts feel impossible.. class stuff piles up.. friends text and i leave it sitting because answering means pretending i am normal

getting out of bed takes forever and then i still show up late or half awake. people at work trust me to cover things and i keep proving i am not up to it. i am the weak person people mean when they talk about someone who can't handle normal life

if i told anyone how bad it is, they would know exactly what i am. lazy, unstable, unreliable. asking for help would just put a stamp on it. loser behavior

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: i read the whole thing. not much to add, but i saw it.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
"not much to add" is fair... there is not much to add to someone being like this

i keep everyone at surface level because the second they know, i become the unreliable one. they already get enough proof when i cancel plans and disappear

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: yeah, disappearing from plans is the part that stood out. that can get noticed pretty fast.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
it does get noticed pretty fast... that is the point

my friends still send little memes and "you alive" texts and i leave them there. replying means explaining why i am always tired and behind, and then i am not just busy, i am the flaky friend for real

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: the "you alive" texts sound like they keep coming in. people do notice patterns.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
people do notice patterns... mine is obvious

roommate sees dishes sit and laundry sit and me going straight to bed after work. i act casual in the kitchen like i am just sleepy. it is embarrassing because this is basic adult stuff and i still fail it

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: that is a lot of day-to-day stuff in one place. work, school, roommate things.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
work, school, roommate things... yeah, all the normal pieces

other people manage the same pieces and still answer texts and clean up and go to class. i watch everyone else keep moving and i am a different category of person. slower, weaker, not trusted with much

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: you keep comparing it to everyone else managing. that came through clearly.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
yeah, comparing it to everyone else managing is exactly where my head stays

because they are managing. i am not. saying it out loud would not fix anything, it would just make people file me under person who cannot handle being counted on. so i stay quiet and let the texts rot. coward version of adult

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
missed my morning class again... not even because anything happened.. i was awake and still stayed in bed until it was too late

there's a group chat for an assignment and i watched the little messages stack up. someone tagged me about my part and i put the phone face down. answering means admitting i have done nothing, and then i am exactly the dead weight people hate getting paired with

same thing at work after. i smiled through a shift like i am fine while being useless inside. everyone else has the normal amount of tired and still functions. i do not. weak link, full stop

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: the group chat part is pretty specific. getting tagged makes it harder to stay invisible.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
getting tagged does make it harder to stay invisible... that is why i muted it

if i answer now, the whole thing turns into me explaining why i am behind. there is no good version of that. i become the person nobody wants on the project because i cannot be trusted with one small part

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: muting it keeps the phone quiet. the messages still sit there.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
the messages still sit there... yeah, and that is the cleanest proof

normal people just send the file or say what is done. i have nothing done. opening the chat is just walking into a room where everyone can see i am the weak one holding them back

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: you keep coming back to the project making it visible.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
the project making it visible is the whole problem...

when it stays in my room it can look like being busy. the second other people need me, it turns into facts. late, empty, not dependable. that is who i am when anyone looks close

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: being needed by other people seems to be the part you are focusing on.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
being needed by other people is exactly where i fail...

work is the same. i can pass for normal until someone asks me to cover a rush or remember closing stuff. then the blank face comes out and someone else fixes it. i am useful until anything requires a real person

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: work and the class project are both about people counting on you.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
people counting on me is the part i keep proving wrong...

if i told my group or my manager anything, it would not explain it. it would confirm they got stuck with someone who cannot handle basic pressure. i stay quiet because quiet is the only way to waste less of their time. dead weight with a schedule

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
the group finally met in person for the assignment today... i walked to the building, saw two of them at a table, and turned around before they saw me

i had my notebook in my bag with one empty page in it. sitting down would mean putting that empty page in front of them and making the whole thing obvious. i left and bought a vending machine coffee i did not want like that counts as being a student

they are doing the work around me now. i am not behind in a cute stressed way. i am the person who hides when people need something. weak, unreliable, extra weight

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: you got as far as the building and then left before the table.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
got as far as the building is the stupid part... i can perform almost normal until the actual people are there

the table made it real. walking up to it meant letting them see i had nothing. i am the empty spot in the group pretending to be a member

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: the empty notebook seems like the thing you did not want them to see.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
the empty notebook was the honest version of me... nothing in it, no excuse attached

if i said i'm not doing well, it turns into the same picture with extra words. people hear that and know i cannot handle basic things

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: you keep the explanation out of it.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
keeping the explanation out of it is cleaner... explaining makes it worse because then it sounds like i want credit for failing slowly

people who can actually handle life do not need a speech for one class project. i do. that puts me on the wrong side of normal

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: the meeting made the difference between private and visible.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
private and visible, yeah... in my room it can still be mess, laundry, unopened tabs

at the table it becomes me. the one who cannot show up with even a page. that is why i keep skipping and letting the chat move without me

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: letting the chat move without you also leaves them making plans around the gap.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
making plans around the gap is what they have to do... the gap is me

i can answer and ask for help, which is just handing them proof that i am useless and making them be polite about it. staying gone wastes less of their time. weak little performance

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
the shared doc has my name sitting there with a blank space under it now... they tagged me this morning asking if i can add my part by tonight

i saw the preview and did not open it. opening it means the read receipt, the little proof that i am awake and still choosing nothing. the deadline is tomorrow and i have one half sentence in my notes app that says "intro maybe" like a clown

asking for help now is just putting a label on it for them: unreliable person, do not trust with work. i am already that without the label. useless extra tab

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: being tagged put your name right next to the blank part.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
right next to the blank part is exactly it... there is no way to make that look like anything else

my name is the part that did not happen. the blank space is more honest than any message i could send

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: the message would make it active instead of just sitting there.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
active is the problem... sitting there at least lets everyone work around me without hearing my little excuse

once i type anything, i become the person asking people to carry me and pretend it is fine. that is worse

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: not typing anything leaves them guessing around the missing section.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
guessing around the missing section still gives them room to be practical... they can split it up and move on

if i answer, they have to deal with me directly. then it is not a missing section, it is me being the weak part of the project

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: the project makes the missing part visible to more than just you.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
visible to more than just me is why i keep everything small and quiet... class, work, roommate, all of it

people can deal with tired if it stays private. they cannot deal with someone who keeps proving they cannot do basic adult things

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: the deadline tomorrow gives it a set time instead of just a vague thing.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
the set time makes it clean... tomorrow they get the proof on schedule

normal people need an extension sometimes. i need a different personality. letting them see me now is worse than staying quiet

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
they submitted the project last night without my part... someone else wrote two paragraphs where mine was supposed to be

now the doc has comments resolved and my name is still in the edit history doing nothing. i skipped class and sat in the bathroom by the vending machines until the bus came back around

this is what happens when people trust me with normal stuff. they get extra work and i hide like a little rat. useless person with a backpack

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: the edit history keeps a record of who touched it and who didn't.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
yeah the record is the worst part... it is cleaner than any excuse

it shows everyone did something and i did not. no mood explanation changes that. i am the missing worker with a timestamp

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: the timestamp makes it pretty exact.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
pretty exact, yeah... exact enough that there is no soft version

not busy, not confused, not unlucky. awake at 1:12 and still not doing it. that is just unreliable

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: being awake then shows up differently than being offline.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
different and worse... offline could be anything

awake means i had the chance and still made everyone carry it. that is the part people remember. not tired. weak

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: now you have class with the same people after it happened.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
after it happened is why i stayed away... walking in would make it a whole scene even if nobody said anything

they would see the person who made them scramble sitting there with coffee like i belong. i do not belong in that room right now

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: not going keeps the room separate from the project for today.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
separate for today is all i can do... keep class there, keep work there, keep my roommate seeing the normal version in the kitchen

if i tell anyone, it becomes real in their face. asking now would be making them say it politely while i stand there being the thing they already know. i am the one people plan around because i break basic things

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
had class again today after the project thing... professor said same groups for the next small assignment unless someone has a reason to change

everyone from my group sat together and i sat two rows back like a ghost with a tote bag. i left before the end so nobody had to do the polite look-at-me part

asking to switch or explain now just makes it official that i am the weak link. they already worked around me once. unreliable person in public

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: same groups makes the project carry into the next thing.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
yeah, carry into the next thing is exactly it... it follows them into the next doc with my name already meaning dead space

they do not need to ask if i will show up. the answer is sitting in the last file. i am the spot people cover before it collapses

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: the last file is still there for everyone to open.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
still there, yeah... and it is neat, which makes it worse

no messy story, no dramatic emergency, just their edits and my blank part. needing help after that is not help, it is proof i cannot handle basic college work

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: a blank section is pretty visible in a shared doc.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
pretty visible is why i kept my screen angled down today... i could feel my face doing that fake calm thing

people who can do the work sit there and talk about due dates. i sit there hoping nobody says my name. different kind of person

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: keeping the screen angled down avoids some attention.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
avoids some attention, yeah... attention is the whole danger

if one person says are you okay, then i have to stand there as the answer. i am not okay and i am not someone who deserves extra explaining around

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: a question like that would put it out loud.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
out loud is the part i cannot let happen... once it is said, i stop being the quiet person in class and become the one everyone has to manage

i can keep sitting far away and leaving early. that is the only useful thing i do now. weak link staying out of the way

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
next assignment started in the same group chat tonight... professor posted the little slide thing and one person tagged me like "can you do the intro part"

i stared at it for twenty minutes and muted the chat. answering would be pretending i am reliable. saying i cannot do it would make the whole weak link thing official again

the only clean thing is staying silent so they can plan around the hole. dead weight with notifications off

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: a tag in the group chat puts your name right in the middle of it.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
right in the middle of it, yeah... that is the worst part

in class i can sit back and make myself smaller. in the chat my name sits there with nothing under it. i am the empty spot everybody can see

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: muting it keeps it from popping up, but the thread is still there.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
the thread is still there... exactly

muted just means i do not have to watch the little number climb. it does not change what it says about me. i am the person a group has to chase and then replace

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: an unanswered tag can stand out on its own.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
stand out on its own, yeah... no explanation needed
